info.name: Task Categories API
info.description:
The buckets a company files work under — Bug, Feature, Operations and whatever else the business actually tracks.

Categories are company configuration, so unlike /tasks these ARE role-gated: an HOD assigns work, an admin decides what the buckets are.

Plan gate: tasks.categories on the writes only. A company on a plan without custom categories still files work under the six seeded defaults, so every GET and /seed-defaults stay open.

request.description: Returns true/false to show or hide the 'Create Default Categories' button during onboarding.
What seeding will create, so the panel can show it before the admin commits.

response.name: OK

request.description: Creates the six default categories. Safe to re-run: existing names are left alone, so a company that renamed 'Bug' and lost the rest can pull the missing ones back in.

response.name: Created

request.description: Admin only, and gated on tasks.categories. Names are unique per company, case-insensitively — 'Bug' and 'bug' are the same bucket.

request.description: Open to every authenticated member — the list is needed to render or filter any task board. task_count is every task ever filed under the category, finished or not. Pass active=true to hide retired buckets.

request.description: Rename, recolour, or retire with is_active:false. Retiring keeps existing tasks filed where they are but takes the bucket out of the assignment dropdown — usually what you want instead of deleting.

response.name: OK

request.description: Soft delete, and it refuses while unfinished tasks still use the category — losing a live task's classification while people are looking at it is worse than keeping a bucket around. Finished work is fine: it keeps its category_id.
